verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents first-party outbound webhooks that fire on internal events and send data to external systems. They can be configured through the API, and the docs also cover Signals webhook alert targets and a runbook step that dispatches HTTP requests, so a programmatic consumer can subscribe to events. Missing for 10: a documented catalog of subscribable event types, payload signing/retry semantics, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: FireHydrant enables you to create webhooks that respond to internal events or custom commands to send information to external systems.
You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
Webhook targets on FireHydrant allow alerts to be sent to external destinations via a webhook.
you may want to dispatch an HTTP request from FireHydrant to those systems.
